title: The `flex` Shorthand & Sizing Secrets 🎛️
description: Master `flex: 1`, `flex: auto`, `flex: none`, and how they compute actual sizes.

slides.title: The `flex` Shorthand 🧬
slides.content:
# All Three in One

The `flex` property is a shorthand for `flex-grow`, `flex-shrink`, and `flex-basis` (in that order).

```css
.item {
  flex: 1 1 0%;  /* grow=1, shrink=1, basis=0% */
}
```
You can omit values; missing ones get their defaults. Common patterns:
- `flex: 1;` → `flex: 1 1 0%;`
- `flex: auto;` → `flex: 1 1 auto;`
- `flex: none;` → `flex: 0 0 auto;`
- `flex: 2;` → `flex: 2 1 0%;`

slides.title: `flex: 1` vs `flex: auto` ⚖️

quizData.question: What does `flex: none;` mean?

options.text: Inflexible: item will not grow or shrink; stays at its natural size

quizData.explanation: `flex: none` is equivalent to `flex: 0 0 auto;` – no growing, no shrinking.

slides.title: How Flexbox Calculates Sizes 📐
slides.content:
# The Algorithm in Simple Terms

1. Container size is known.
2. For each item, browser looks at `flex-basis` (or width/height if `auto`).
3. If total basis < container, extra space is distributed according to `flex-grow` ratios.
4. If total basis > container, deficit is removed according to `flex-shrink` ratios (and `min-width`/`max-width` constraints).
5. Final size may be further adjusted by `min/max` properties.

So `flex-basis: 0%` ensures the item has no initial size, making equal distribution from `flex-grow` perfectly equal.

slides.title: Common Shorthand Values
Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Always Use the Shorthand

Prefer `flex` shorthand over individual longhands. It resets unspecified components to their defaults, avoiding unexpected behaviour.
